find: It operates at approximately 230 V and changes direction 50 times per second — a frequency of 50 Hz.
replace: It operates at approximately 230 V and completes 50 cycles every second — a frequency of 50 Hz. The current changes direction twice in each cycle, so it reverses 100 times every second.
note: F7: 50 Hz is 50 complete cycles per second. Each cycle contains two reversals, so the mains current changes direction 100 times a second, not 50. P2.2.4 requires learners to recall 50 Hz and explain the difference between direct and alternating voltage.

find: This produces an alternating current (a.c.) — the voltage reverses direction once per revolution of the magnet.
replace: This produces an alternating current (a.c.) — the voltage reverses direction every half turn, so one revolution of the magnet gives one complete cycle.
note: F12: the induced p.d. reverses twice in each revolution, giving one full cycle per turn. The lesson's own flashcard ('reverses its direction of cutting field lines each half-turn') and the mark scheme for practice question 4 both say this correctly, so the content contradicted itself. P3.7.4 asks learners to explain the p.d./time graph of an alternator.
